title: 195 Mitigating enteric methane emissions from grazing beef cattle: Preliminary findings of the implementation of climate-smart practices in South Carolina
content:
Abstract
Cow calf production is one of the largest agricultural activities in South Carolina per unit of land area. Forages are the primary feed source due to favorable climatic conditions, a wide range of adapted species, and access to local resources. Most cow-calf systems are based on perennial grasses, and there is a high reliance on off-farm inputs to support forage production and animal performance. Thus, management strategies are warranted to increase cow-calf production systems’ sustainability, nutrient cycling, resilience, and profitability. Although greenhouse gas mitigation strategies in beef grazing systems are limited, practices that increase productivity (kgs of meat per hectare) while having a minor impact on greenhouse gas (GHG) emission can decrease the emission rates per pound of product (meat) and, in this way, reduce the environmental footprint of beef production. We launched a pilot project to incentivize beef cattle producers to implement selected climate-smart production practices, including prescribed grazing and nutrient management through using chicken manure and incorporating legumes in pastures. The project will also measure and verify the GHG benefits associated with the proposed climate-smart practices while supporting the development of markets for the resulting climate-smart commodities. We will conduct direct measurements in the field of GHG emissions on 10% of the farms enrolled using a portable head chamber gas emission monitoring (GreenFeed; C-Lock Inc., Rapid City, SD). In summary, beef production systems can reduce agricultural GHG emissions and lead to more sustainable agricultural systems. The proposed climate-smart practices in this project will help cow-calf producers in South Carolina adopt new forage management strategies that will reduce environmental impact while increasing the profitability of their livestock operations.
